s1.p1: Well, now we have reached the third fundamental principle of structural programming - loops.
s1.p2: As I hope we already know, a loop is a repetition of the same actions several times.
s1.p3: That is, there is some code that must be executed repeatedly.
s1.p4: This code is placed in curly braces **⟦f0⟧** and is called the **body of the loop**.
s1.p5: Each repetition of the loop is called a **loop iteration**.
s1.p6: Thus, any loop statement will have a body, and this body is always enclosed in curly braces.
s1.p7: But every loop has one important task: to stop at the right time.
s1.p8: We cannot endlessly repeat the execution of the code in curly braces.
s1.p9: An endless loop means a browser tab freezing. We certainly don't need it.
s1.p10: So, we need to stop the loop at the right time.
s1.p11: To do this, determine when the loop should be stopped.
s1.p13: - Directly specify how many times the loop should be executed;
s1.p14: - Set some condition that the loop will be repeated if it is fulfilled. Such a condition (some expression) is always placed in parentheses.
s1.p15: The loop condition can be any evaluated expression (i.e. syntactically correct), but after evaluating the value of this expression, the engine will always cast it to a boolean type (**⟦f1⟧** or **⟦f2⟧**).
s1.p16: So, any loop operator has three mandatory parts: **the operator name** (keyword), a **condition** in parentheses, and a **body** in curly braces.
s1.p17: We begin our journey through loops with the **⟦f3⟧** loop statement.
s1.p18: The **⟦f3⟧** loop operator requires a counter variable (loop variable), which must:
s1.p19: 1. have an initial value. In other words, it must be declared and assigned an initial value;
s1.p20: 2. the variable must change its value after each iteration of the loop (otherwise the loop will be infinite);
s1.p21: 3. at each iteration, the value of the loop variable must be checked against the condition (otherwise the loop will be infinite).

s2.p4: 3. at each iteration, the loop variable's value must be checked to see if the constraint is met (otherwise the loop will be infinite).
